issue.title: sase-core flake: gateway fleet route tests hit fleet read/refresh deadlines under full-suite load (504 / snapshot_refresh timeout)
issue.description:
Proposed by epic phase sase-14s.5 (sase-core "split the ten largest Rust files" epic) as a
PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; filed by the sase-14s land agent. Not caused by sase-14s: that phase
moved crates/sase_gateway/src/routes.rs into a routes/ module tree verbatim (84/84 tests,
44/44 routes identical); no timing, deadline, or handler logic changed.

Repo: sase-core. Tests (post-split paths, sase-core 5154900):
- crates/sase_gateway/src/routes/tests/fleet_attention.rs:351
  `fleet_attention_read_empty_request_touches_no_notification_store` — got 504
  GATEWAY_TIMEOUT instead of 200. 504 is `ApiError::fleet_timeout` ("fleet read timed
  out", routes/errors.rs:453), i.e. a fleet read deadline elapsed.
- crates/sase_gateway/src/routes/tests/fleet_handlers.rs:306
  `fleet_launch_replays_delayed_launch_and_reconciles_visible_row` — timed out waiting
  on snapshot_refresh (the test uses an 80 ms DelayedLaunchBridge).

Both failed once under a full-workspace `just check` (./scripts/check.sh all) with the
whole cargo test suite running in parallel, then passed 3/3 run in isolation and on a
full green `just check` rerun. Likely shared mechanism: fixed wall-clock fleet read /
refresh deadlines in the gateway test state are too tight when the host is CPU-starved.
Diagnose which deadline elapses before choosing a fix (a test-only deadline override,
a larger test budget, or an observable wait); do not weaken the assertions.

task_type_fields.evidence: Failed once each (504 vs 200; snapshot_refresh timeout) in one full-workspace parallel just check; passed 3/3 isolated and on a full green rerun on the same tree. Serial: not reproduced.
task_type_fields.repro_cmd: just check (sase-core ./scripts/check.sh all) under parallel load
